title: AUTH-1 host approval
description: What a host asks a paired device when a PAM password prompt is waiting, and what the device answers. The device signs `nonce` in context; the host never sends, stores or learns the user's password, and it never sends anything the device could replay at another prompt.

device_id.description: The identity this device must sign as: the device_id of the credential this connection authenticated with. It is part of `signed_message` and it is the only signed field the device cannot derive from its own state, so the host states it per device rather than letting the device guess. A device that re-paired holds a newer local id than the credential it still connects with, and a guess there fails every approval with `biometric_signature_invalid`.

nonce.description: 256 bits, single use. The pending record is dropped the moment it is decided, so a second submission with the same signature is refused.

resolved.description: Payload of `auth.approval.resolved`. Sent to every device that was asked, so a card that is no longer answerable goes away by itself.

signed_message.description: The exact bytes a device signs, ASCII, newline separated, with a trailing newline: "omodachi-auth-approval-v1", host_id, approval_id, nonce, service, user, device_id. Every field that scopes the approval is in it, so a signature cannot move between hosts, services, users, devices or prompts.

decision.description: Body of POST /v1/auth/approvals/{approval_id}. `approve` carries a base64 DER ECDSA-P256-SHA256 signature over `signed_message`; `decline` carries nothing, because refusing is the fail-safe direction and the bearer credential is enough to say no.

enrollment.description: Body of POST /v1/auth/keys. `enabled` is the device's own half of AUTH-1's two switches and must be reported explicitly; the signature proves the device holds the private half of `public_key`.

public_key.description: base64 of the uncompressed X9.63 P-256 point (04 || X || Y, 65 bytes), or of its SPKI DER wrapping.

secure_enclave.description: Whether the private key lives in the Secure Enclave. A simulator cannot, and says so rather than pretending.
